facts.statement: The genus name Europasaurus means 'Europe lizard'.

facts.statement: Four frontal bones have been found in Europasaurus, comprising three from the left side and one from the right.

facts.statement: Parietal bones in Europasaurus exhibit a rectangular shape that is significantly wider than long.

facts.statement: The jugals of Europasaurus resemble those of basal sauropodomorphs more closely than those of other macronarians.

facts.statement: The two processes of the quadratojugal bone in Europasaurus diverge at nearly 90 degrees, with the dorsal process curving to match the quadrate.
facts.quote: The two quadratojugal processes diverge at a nearly right angle (90º), although the dorsal process curves as it follows the shape of the quadrate.

facts.statement: The squamosals of Europasaurus have a question-mark-like shape in lateral view, similar to those of Camarasaurus.

facts.statement: Thirteen palate elements, including the quadrate, pterygoid, and ectopterygoid, are preserved in Europasaurus.

facts.statement: The pterygoid is the largest bone in the sauropod palate and has a triradiate shape similar to the postorbital.

facts.statement: Europasaurus vertebrae feature a side excavation that connects to internal air-filled spaces.
facts.quote: In the side of the centra of Europasaurus there is an excavation which opens into the internal pneumaticity of the vertebrae.

facts.statement: Europasaurus possesses a vertically standing neural spine, a primitive trait absent in Brachiosaurus and more advanced sauropods.

facts.statement: The sacrum of Europasaurus consists of five fused vertebrae, a count typical of basal neosauropods.
facts.quote: All five vertebrae, the characteristic number of more basal neosauropods, are incorporated into the sacrum.

facts.statement: Fossilized skin impressions of Europasaurus relatives show scales but lack bony plates or nodules that would indicate armor.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Europasaurus is a true brachiosaurid, as some analyses place it there despite the lack of key diagnostic bones like caudal vertebrae.
